Fashion / Style

Fashion is already being served at this year’s U.S. Open

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:11
Instaread

WORDS Cassandra Dimitroff    PHOTOGRAPHY courtesy U.S. Open    PUBLISHED Tue, 1 Sep 2026 - 11:15 am

There aren't many sports with as much fashion history as tennis. From the legacy of Wimbledon whites to tennis-inspired fashion trends, the relationship between the sartorial and the court has grown narrower and narrower. Just ask Naomi Osaka, who has blown the doors off the sport and re-written its fashion rules. And this week, with the U.S. Open kicking off in New York City, there's plenty more fashion to keep in focus.

We aren't too far into the tournament yet, but there are already some standouts – from Sabalenka's 127-carat gold necklace to Townsend's beaded bodysuit. These are the on-court fashion moments from this year's U.S. Open that we're already talking about...

 

Naomi Osaka

Our expectations were high for Osaka – and she did not disappoint. For her first outing at the US Open, the tennis star was styled by Law Roach, in a custom piece by Who Decides Wear.

 

Aryna Sabalenka

Sabalenka beat out Osorio in her first match as she begins to defend her title at this year's U.S. Open. She wore an orange, netted Nike dress with a custom 127-carat gold The Prism necklace by Material Good, adorned with vibrant multi-coloured gemstones like sapphires, tourmalines and tanzanites. She wore the necklace and matching earrings for an earlier match, too.

 

Taylor Townsend

The American professional tennis player and former world No. 1  wore a black, red and white striped dress completed with beaded fringe. Many fans thought this look was in honour of her playing on Trinidad and Tobago's Independence Day (which falls on 31 August).

 

Zheng Qinwen

Qinwen won her opening match in a turquoise and white Nike fit, complete with matching turquoise sweat bands and tennis shoes.

 

Sára Bejlek

Bejlek, the 20-year-old professional tennis player from the Czech Republic, won her opening round game in a matching neon pink ensemble. But her hair was where the magic happened: a bubble ponytail complete with rhinestone stars and barrets.

 

Iva Jovic

adidas kitted out Iva Jovic for her U.S. Open first match, where she walked out in a plum-toned bubble skirt and matching jacket and visor. The jacket was later shed to reveal a cut-out white bodysuit.

Fashion / Fashion News

The Met’s planned John Galliano exhibition has been cancelled

WORDS Kirsty Thatcher    PHOTOGRAPHY from 'High & Low: John Galliano'    PUBLISHED Tue, 1 Sep 2026 - 4:36 am

The Metropolitan Museum of Art will no longer stage its planned exhibition dedicated to John Galliano, ending months of speculation around what was set to be one of the most significant fashion retrospectives of 2027.

The exhibition, which was announced in July, was intended to examine the designer’s career across four decades, from his Central Saint Martins graduation collection in 1984 to his work at Givenchy, Dior and Maison Margiela. It would have brought together clothing, accessories, sketches and archival material, offering an unusually comprehensive look at one of fashion’s most influential, and complicated, figures.

Instead, the exhibition has been called off following discussions between Galliano and the Met.

 

Why was the John Galliano exhibition cancelled?

The decision comes amid continued debate over how Galliano’s legacy should be remembered following the antisemitic and racist remarks he made in 2011.

Although his influence on contemporary fashion is impossible to dispute, the announcement of a retrospective celebrating his work was met with a mix of criticism and enthusiasm.

His career spans some of the industry’s most important houses and eras, and this would have been only the third Costume Institute retrospective dedicated to a living designer, following Yves Saint Laurent in 1983 and Rei Kawakubo in 2017.

The cancellation therefore raises a larger question about how fashion institutions approach designers whose creative legacies exist alongside serious personal controversies.

In a statement, Galliano said, “After much reflection and discussion with The Met and all those involved, I have decided, with great sadness, that it is best for the exhibition not to take place at this time. I remain fully accountable for the pain caused by my words in the past, particularly the hurt I caused to the Jewish and Asian communities, and I remain deeply sorry for it. I understand that meaningful atonement is not achieved through an exhibition, institutional recognition or a single public gesture. It is a continuing responsibility, demonstrated through listening, learning and one’s conduct over time.”

Anna Wintour, who supported the proposed exhibition, has also backed Galliano’s decision to withdraw it.

In a statement, Wintour called the decision courageous, saying, "I believe this is the right decision, and both he and the Museum have my full support."

Her comments make clear the tension at the centre of the proposed exhibition: whether artistic legacy can – or should – be separated from accountability. For now, the Met appears to have decided that this particular retrospective is not the place to resolve it.

 

What will happen to the 2027 Met Gala?

The 2027 Met Gala itself has not been cancelled. Rather, the exhibition it was expected to accompany will no longer go ahead. The Met has said that details of a replacement Spring 2027 Costume Institute exhibition, along with the theme for the 2027 Met Gala, will be announced at a later date.

Watch this space.
